claims.statement: The host-only Harbor migration changes Talos host resolution to a dedicated Traefik registry Service while preserving live registry mirror configuration and unrelated hosts; execution is guarded by route validation and exact reviewed main.

Harbor's fixed Traefik scope selects the ingress image and exact pause:3.10 native pull probe from the reviewed full catalog, preserves all-platform digests and tag aliases, and requires fresh complete authenticated Harbor pulls with robot$mirror+pull; callers cannot choose images or destinations, and scoped success does not establish global mirror coverage.

Full-catalog Talos mirror verification requires a successful workflow run titled Mirror all @ followed by that run's full head SHA and an unchanged publication bundle, rejecting scoped, untitled and mismatched-revision runs. An ordinary execute also requires supplied reader auth or captured exact valid robot$mirror+pull auth; otherwise it stops before candidate configuration or apply.

The Traefik registry listener admits only four fixed Talos LAN addresses, four individual cni0 bridges, four flannel.1 overlay addresses as unauthenticated sources, and the exact automation/renovate principal as an authenticated source on port 9443; whole Pod CIDRs remain excluded, routing remains OCI/token-only, and Flannel NetworkPolicy is not enforced.

The staged cutover requires registry policy convergence and successful uncached image pulls from every node before advancing Harbor DNS; the October 10 failed first pull and unresolved zimaboard-2 reboot do not establish rollout success or durable node recovery.

The Talos Harbor helper reads the complete machineconfig resource stream, requires active v1alpha1, permits a missing persistent resource only for version1 STATE boot, and otherwise requires semantic equality of all active/persistent documents before changing the host mapping.

The October 11 zimaboard-2 host-only pull timed out with six destination ztunnel denials from overlay source 10.244.4.0 and no Traefik requests; the exact overlay source fix requires GitOps convergence and correlated successful registry requests before rollout acceptance.

The runbook records October 11 and 19 full-catalog failures on LiteLLM's repeated-descriptor index and Harbor's correlated unique_reference error. The fixed LiteLLM scope stages the exact Linux amd64 child while the current consumer pin stays intact; only after a scoped pull receipt may a separate PR switch the consumer and remove the failing index from the full catalog, followed by a full-catalog retry. No live schema repair or strict mirror activation follows from scoped publication alone.

The maintained Harbor v2.15.4 core candidate verifies a pinned source archive and patches the manager to persist identical child relations once while rejecting differing digest/platform/URL/annotation metadata before any DAO write; its repair preserves the artifact digest and descriptors and changes no registry bytes or database schema.

The core candidate uses a pinned Chainguard Go builder, upstream-pinned Swagger generation and an upstream runtime payload; its build must reproduce the original duplicate-reference failure before passing repaired manager tests and complete core compilation, with networking disabled for tests/build after dependency download.

The held core candidate changes no active consuming references, credential producers or live database. It also stages an excluded namespace pull contract; activation still requires Linux/registry/scan acceptance, protected publication, reviewed component/chart compatibility and verified backups.

The candidate build invokes a disposable pinned Harbor v2.15.4 stack without host ports on an internal service network. Its test client shares the proxy network namespace and uses loopback, while proxy and jobservice await core health. It requires unchanged push/pull of an eight-descriptor repeated OCI index and all child content plus exactly one PostgreSQL relation, then cleans fixture-owned credentials and resources without production inputs.

The dated 2026-10-11 base-scan receipt records an unfiltered Grype 0.112.0 audit of the hash-verified upstream Harbor v2.15.4 Photon 5.0 runtime base with a valid fresh database: 32 Go package matches across 26 advisory IDs, including three critical and 15 high matches, with 26 fixed, four not-fixed and two unknown fix states. It explicitly does not establish rebuilt-candidate or deployed-workload CVE clearance.

The sanitized 2026-10-11 registry fixture receipt records successful candidate CI at e3f58417, including Linux image build, original failure and repaired manager tests, unchanged registry push/pull of eight descriptors plus child manifest and every blob, and one PostgreSQL parent/child relation. It retains the job URL, source head, index digest and log hash while denying publication, deployment and CVE-clearance acceptance.

The third Harbor source patch requires Go 1.27.2, upgrades the reported NTLM/networking/crypto/Helm/telemetry/compression dependencies, and replaces gorilla/csrf with filippo.io/csrf/gorilla. Browser origin/Fetch metadata enforce CSRF while legacy response token headers, the declared key contract, invalid-key refusal and non-session API exemption remain; tokens no longer provide the check and nonbrowser requests are allowed.

The dated rebuilt Linux binary scan receipt records five remaining matches with no finding exclusions: four Distribution v2 advisories and one x/crypto advisory, all unfixed/unknown, with two high, two medium and one unknown severity. It explicitly denies final-container or deployed-digest CVE clearance.

The local remediated core assessment retains all five raw Grype matches while recording absence of affected OpenPGP and Distribution proxy/storage/handler packages from its compiled graph, a module-only OpenPGP finding from Go binary analysis, and a native positive/negative JWK verifier test rejecting attacker key material under a forged trusted key ID. Build guards preserve these specific conditions; the receipt denies final-image and other-component clearance.

After the Linux registry fixture, the candidate CI scans the complete Docker-saved runtime archive with lock-pinned Grype 0.112.0. The report checker validates exact image/config identity, Linux amd64/Photon 5.0, fresh valid database/report and no exclusions/filtering/VEX, refusing available fixes while retaining unresolved counts. A sanitized identity/hash/database/severity receipt is emitted; raw metadata stays private, temporary inputs are cleaned, and collection success does not grant CVE clearance or publication.

The full-container receipt records successful candidate Linux audit at279092e6 with exact image config identity and five unfiltered unresolved matches (two high, two medium, one unknown), passing the available-fix refusal gate while explicitly denying CVE clearance.

The active Harbor Kustomization stages a namespace-local Docker-config ExternalSecret from the existing read-only robot parameter, referenced by the vulnerability exporter only for kubelet image pulls. The excluded private-core candidate holds a ServiceAccount pull reference. No new IAM/SSM declaration or credential rotation is added; core activation still requires reviewed publication/scans, recovery clearance, ExternalSecret readiness, and cold-bootstrap safeguards.

The dispatch-only protected core publisher accepts only exact current main and its dedicated workflow, builds and audits before credentials, and requires zero matches in the exact full-container Grype report before publication. It publishes one fixed core reference, completely pulls and verifies its digest before signing, and verifies destination signatures against the enrolled key before emitting a pinned artifact. Core signer Pods use the Harbor Cosign mirror; NOFX remains two-subject and release/recovery gates remain.

Both publication catalogs list thirteen digest-pinned cgr.dev/chainguard/* sources. Go, nginx, Node runtime, Node dev, static, and Wolfi base are the six additions to the prior seven-image receipt, so expanded publication requires protected production approval and complete authenticated Harbor-pull acceptance.

Missing mirror artifacts normally stage all platforms anonymously and verify the original root digest before Harbor upload. For the exact Skopeo digest-preserving OCI conversion error during staging or upload, regctl copies the pinned source digest, including a second upstream read after failed upload. A resumed digest can similarly use regctl for a failing alias copy. Both paths require exact digest and alias verification plus a fresh complete authenticated Harbor pull; unrelated copy errors fail closed.

The full catalog contains digest-pinned kube-network-policies v1.1.2 and paused Argo CD Image Updater v1.3.0. Cataloging activates no enforcer; activation requires repository-owned Talos NRI configuration, live socket/plugin registration, negative startup/bypass tests, NetworkPolicy review, and a fail-closed strict-mode worker canary.

The core publication workflow tests the pinned public Chainguard Cosign candidate before registry credentials, then runs every core signing-Pod container from the same digest mirrored in Harbor. The 2026-10-11 receipt proves a complete Harbor pull of the exact multi-platform image (two manifests, 18 blobs), but does not prove source-signature transfer or record Linux compatibility acceptance.

The reviewed Stage A saved plan created and metadata-verified /homelab/harbor/mirror-robot-pull-password without reading its value, limited to the reader parameter and exact-ARN reader-policy changes, including deterministic policy chunk creation or rebalancing. It requires stack generation before reader-plan review and separate approval for wider shared closure. Stage B desired state advances harbor-secrets OnChange revision to v4 and mounts the reader key in Harbor bootstrap; after External Secrets materializes the target Secret, a bootstrap execution can create or patch the reader robot, while ExternalSecret Ready and successful PostSync are required before acceptance. Stage A alone establishes no robot, receipt, Talos, workload, or privacy acceptance, and mirror remains public until authenticated node pulls pass before a separate reviewed privacy change.

Mastodon's fixed four-image publication scope uses its separate PostgreSQL 18-bookworm security candidate without changing Harbor's existing database pin, and requires all-platform digest copies, aliases and complete authenticated Harbor pulls before consuming references merge.

Hosted Harbor publication CI forwards the disposable runner to traefik/traefik-private over a bounded Kubernetes port-forward with the Octelium CI credential, maps the Harbor hostname to loopback, and retains TLS verification.

The full Harbor catalog stages the newer digest-pinned Dispatcharr and n8n sources while retaining their former digests for rollback. The consuming Renovate PRs remain held until protected publication and complete authenticated Harbor pulls verify the new destinations.

The full Harbor catalog stages nine Harbor 2.15.4 component digests beside active 2.15.2 entries without changing running Pods; protected fixed Harbor-scope publication and authenticated pull acceptance precede the separate consumer upgrade, which must preserve singleton nginx rolling-update availability. The scoped receipt does not prove full-catalog coverage while the LiteLLM duplicate-index failure remains.

The native Harbor receipt scan robot depends on /homelab/harbor/robot-scan-password and an exact-ARN External Secrets reader grant. Read-only inspection verified the version 1 SecureString and grant, and a targeted plan from main at f6506136 found no changes on 2026-10-18. The parameter alone creates no robot or receipt.

Harbor registry uses Recreate, so the 2.15.4 registry and registryctl container images must be cached on every node before the consumer merge. The repository-owned Talos operator selects exactly two reviewed pins, requires exact current main for execution, verifies CRI cache aliases after pull, and supports read-only cache audit. Cache proof does not establish live rollout health.

The staged Harbor-only admission policy uses Warn and Audit for Pod image references, including init and ephemeral containers; Deny is held until live inventory, protected publication, and authenticated node-pull acceptance.

Cordium runner publication is staged behind an exact-main manual dispatch for a fixed runner/controller image pair with authenticated Harbor pulls and signatures; live publication and cold-pull acceptance remain pending while the pool is disabled.

The fixed Renovate Harbor publication scope selects seven reviewed catalog entries for Fleet, Harbor PostgreSQL, Multica Python, Dispatcharr, Bazarr, n8n, and the Renovate runner. It uses all-platform digest, alias, and complete authenticated pull checks; a scoped receipt proves only those seven images.

The protected native receipt uses local OCI layouts for complete source and authenticated Harbor downloads, compares root index bytes and required platform descriptors, and requests Harbor's exact vulnerability report type for child scans. Pull-request lint has no commit-status write permission, leaving the trusted base provenance workflow to set the receipt status.

The fixed dns Harbor mirror scope selects only the pinned Codeberg k8s_gateway image. Protected run 39161113974 succeeded at exact main 5558f8c1 with matching digest and complete authenticated pull; this scoped receipt does not prove full-catalog or live resolver health.

The suspended Renovate CronJob uses a dedicated ServiceAccount without a mounted Kubernetes API token and resolves the canonical Harbor hostname to the registry-only Traefik Service at 10.96.0.50:443; Istio allows that identity only on the registry port 9443.

The first in-cluster Renovate dry run was rejected by destination ztunnel under its default service identity before Harbor traffic reached Traefik; the registry-only route requires a later post-convergence Job and credential review before writer cutover.

The fixed LiteLLM mirror scope selects only the digest-pinned Linux amd64 child of the repeated-index source, stages it beside the unchanged current runtime index pin, and requires a complete authenticated Harbor pull before a separate consumer/catalog change and full-catalog retry; this scoped receipt alone does not authorize strict Talos mirrors.
